clue.text: Discontinued article woman wanted available now

parts.note: something discontinued has been taken off, so off
the is the definite article
Peg is a woman's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: A dropped line of clothing a shopper wanted turns out to be in stock after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes bought off the peg are ready-made, so they can be had at once rather than made to order.

clue.text: Ford, perhaps chasing very big film award

indicators.note: chasing means the car comes after the outsize piece

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very big
a Ford is an example of a car

explanation.surface: Harrison Ford going after a top movie prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like Harrison Ford the actor, but it is the car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the popular name for the Academy Award for film.

clue.text: Catching fish in the country, without regular work?

indicators.note: catching means the country holds the fish within it

parts.note: France is a country
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Fishing in rural parts with no steady job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' reads as rural areas; it is France.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for different clients rather than holding one regular job.

clue.text: Passes over workers in low position

parts.note: hands are manual workers
down is a low position

explanation.surface: Staff in a lowly spot handing things on.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand down something is to pass it over to a successor, as an heirloom.

clue.text: What really ought not to include improper fractions?

definitions.text: What really ought not to include improper fractions?

parts.words: What really ought not to include improper fractions?
parts.note: improper is read as impure, so the discipline untainted by applications should exclude them

explanation.definitionFit: Pure mathematics is maths studied for its own sake, which jokingly ought to be free of anything improper.

clue.text: Dog that's good and ancient, a fetching creature

parts.note: olden means of old, ancient
a retriever is an animal that fetches things back

explanation.surface: A pet that is fine, elderly and attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fetching' looks like attractive but means bringing back.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden retriever is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Daughter's desire to give up

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's is the link to what follows
an itch is a restless craving or desire

explanation.surface: A girl's longing to quit something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch a plan or habit is informally to abandon it, a close synonym.

clue.text: 5 proceed in secret

parts.note: 5 refers to the answer at 5 down, which is a dog
to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: A cross-reference instructs one to move on quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: To lie doggo is to stay hidden and quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggo, as in lie doggo, means hidden or out of sight, keeping secret.

clue.text: Indeed attempt to grab half of -haul

indicators.note: to grab means the attempt word takes hold of letters inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: half of means the second half of the word haul is used

explanation.surface: An attempt to seize part of a haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Truly and indeed are both adverbs of emphasis meaning in fact.

clue.text: A centre for Dutch elm virus spreading south of Hague capital

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means placed below, so after
capital means the initial letter of the word Hague
spreading means the letters of elm virus are scattered

explanation.surface: A Dutch elm disease spreading southward from The Hague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges ELMVIRUS into ILVERSUM, set below H.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilversum is a Dutch town that is the centre of the Netherlands' broadcasting.

clue.text: Char carbon of poorer quality

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
lean in the sense of meagre or poor gives leaner as its comparative

explanation.surface: Burnt carbon of an inferior grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A char, short for charwoman, is a British term for a domestic cleaner.

clue.text: The French hoax about Parisian capital? Could be

definitions.text: The French hoax about Parisian capital? Could be

parts.note: le is the French masculine for the

indicators.note: about means the word gull goes round the letter that follows

parts.note: to gull is to dupe or hoax someone

indicators.note: capital here means the capital, or initial, letter of the word Parisian

explanation.surface: A trick played in France concerning money from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue serves as definition: a French joke wrapped round P could indeed be this kind of hoax.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-pull is a playful hoax or joke at someone's expense, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Australian football strips

definitions.meaning: Aussie ... is the Australian code of football
printers' ... are thin strips of metal used to print lines

explanation.definitionFit: Australian rules football is called Rules for short, and a rule is also a thin strip of metal or wood.

clue.text: Men's money scattered for goddess

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of the two words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Men's cash is spread around in tribute to a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Mnemosyne is the Greek goddess of memory and mother of the Muses.

clue.text: Gold miners coming around high mountain

indicators.note: coming around means the two pieces are turned to read backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Gold prospectors coming round a lofty peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming around' turns the whole gold-plus-miners run backwards. A Munro is any Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet, named after Sir Hugh Munro who listed them.
explanation.definitionFit: Munros are Scottish peaks above 3,000 feet, so each is a high mountain.

clue.text: What gives the volume in a cone?

definitions.text: What gives the volume in a cone?

parts.words: What gives the volume in a cone?
parts.note: volume is read as loudness rather than the geometry of a cone's capacity

explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone-shaped device that amplifies the voice, adding loudness.

clue.text: Becoming late, strained terribly to gain seconds

indicators.note: terribly means the letters of strained are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone running late strains badly to gain a few seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges STRAINED into TARDINES; 'to gain' adds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is the state of lateness; 'becoming late' is read as a noun phrase for it.

clue.text: Cutting off liaison to unfortunate

indicators.note: unfortunate means the letters of liaison to are in a bad, disordered state

explanation.surface: Ending a relationship to an unlucky partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolation is separation from others, the state of being cut off.

clue.text: Curate dealt in a roundabout way with his host

indicators.note: dealt in a roundabout way means the letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman deals indirectly with the person entertaining him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like a person entertaining guests; it is the consecrated bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The host is the consecrated bread of Holy Communion, which is also called the Eucharist.

clue.text: Something about London judo : practitioner

definitions.meaning: the protected countryside ring round London
a judoka of a mid grade wears this coloured belt

explanation.definitionFit: The green belt is the protected countryside ring encircling London, and a judo student of that grade is a green belt.

clue.text: William becoming possessive when it comes to his razor?

definitions.text: William becoming possessive when it comes to his razor?

parts.words: William becoming possessive when it comes to his razor?
parts.note: the medieval philosopher William, whose name takes a possessive in the famous principle called his razor

explanation.definitionFit: William of Occam, the English philosopher, is known through the principle called Occam's razor.

clue.text: Native dropping a storage chest in sudden fear almost

indicators.note: in means the chest and a are placed inside the shortened fear word
almost means the last letter of the fear word is lopped off

parts.note: panic is a sudden overwhelming fear
kist is a Scottish word for a chest or coffer

explanation.surface: A local drops a storage trunk in a near panic.
explanation.walkthrough: PANIC less its last letter is PANI; KIST and A go into it to give PA-KISTA-NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pakistani is a native of Pakistan.

clue.text: Time to financially exploit rising Austrian artist

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to milk is to exploit for money

explanation.surface: Time to cash in on an up-and-coming Viennese painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Klimt was an Austrian painter of the Vienna Secession.

clue.text: Produce wicket in time?

indicators.note: in means the wicket letter goes inside the time word

parts.note: a span is a stretch of time
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A bowler asks whether a wicket might come in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: To spawn is to produce or generate, as fish produce eggs.

clue.text: Area yielded source of tequila

parts.note: to give way is to yield, so gave means yielded

explanation.surface: A region that produced the plant behind Mexico's spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is distilled from the blue agave, a succulent plant of Mexico.

clue.text: Valuable piece that may be soaring

definitions.meaning: a former United States ten-dollar gold coin
a large bird of prey that soars high

explanation.definitionFit: An eagle was a ten-dollar US gold coin, and the eagle is a soaring bird of prey.

clue.text: A folder should keep this work neat

definitions.text: A folder should keep this work neat

parts.words: A folder should keep this work neat
parts.note: a folder is read as someone who folds paper, whose craft needs tidy creases

explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes, done by a folder.

clue.text: Making speech in French here is no good

parts.note: voici is French for here is

explanation.surface: Giving a talk in French when it isn't going well.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicing an opinion is uttering it, so voicing means making speech.

clue.text: What's taken in school for oral English

indicators.note: oral means the school's name is spoken out loud, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: What's studied at a school for spoken English.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the English public school near Windsor; said aloud it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eaten has been taken in as food, so the past participle fits 'taken'.

clue.text: Thin band round neck horses must have to tether

parts.note: a string is a stable's group of racehorses
to tie is to tether

explanation.surface: A halter for horses must be fastened round the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A string tie is a very narrow necktie, often worn in a bow.
